scope: CVG-002B2B signed synthetic PIX inbound and durable shared-B1 settlement worker

criteria.description: The bounded B2b synthetic inbound/shared-B1 worker slice, its owners and dependencies are explicit and non-overlapping with B2a, B2c, real providers and production.
criteria.limitations: Only reversible repository code, disposable PostgreSQL and the explicit local synthetic provider are in scope; B2c SPA/E2E, real provider contracts, credentials, external mutation, production, deployment and release remain excluded.

criteria.description: The raw-body protocol, canonical claims and fingerprints, tenant authority, attempt states, receipt/delivery schemas, service-principal policy, ACL/RLS durability, shared no-replay worker transaction, lock order, retry/fencing machine, rollback and legacy boundary are frozen enough for a coherent implementation.
criteria.limitations: The current code still contains the legacy/current seams named by the contract; this gate authorizes the RED/GREEN implementation work that must replace or isolate them. It is not evidence that migration 0111, the shared primitive, ACL changes or worker exist.

criteria.description: The RED-first files and executable checks cover raw socket/HMAC behavior, canonicalization, attempt preconditions, replay/divergence, two tenants, RLS/least privilege after reconciler reruns, service login/cache/MFA exclusion, B1 lock/staging, worker fencing/restart/rollback, production fail-closed, legacy boundaries, dedicated coverage, regressions and security review.
criteria.limitations: The baseline B1 is green, but B2b REDs, dedicated coverage and behavior are not yet executed; later implementation and verification gates are mandatory.

authority.scope: CVG-002B2B signed synthetic PIX inbound and durable shared-B1 settlement worker
authority.decision: Authorize reversible repository implementation, disposable PostgreSQL and an explicitly local synthetic PIX provider for the bounded B2b inbound receipt/shared-B1 worker slice; real providers, credentials, external mutation, production, deployment and release remain excluded.
authority.expires_or_revalidates: Revalidate before real provider contracts, credentials, external mutation, production ACL/deployment, irreversible migration, operational redrive authority or release acceptance; revalidate after changes to protocol, attempt/delivery states, lock order, service-principal policy, shared UoW, runtime grants or coverage configuration.

next_action: Write and execute the first rejecting B1/B2 attempt-reservation test before implementing migration, shared transaction primitive or B2b production code.
revalidation_triggers: Any expansion from local synthetic provider/reversible code/disposable PostgreSQL to real provider, credentials, external mutation, production, deployment or release
Changes to attempt accepted states, claims canonicalization/fingerprint domains, delivery lease/CAS/backoff/max-attempt rules or billing-to-PIX-to-attempt lock order
Changes to service-principal login/cache/MFA filters, runtime ACL reconciler/init/Helm behavior or the shared no-replay worker transaction
A RED, role regression, coverage seam, security scan or independent review disproves the bounded readiness assumptions
